questions.question: What is a model's context window?
options: Everything the model can see in one request, measured in tokens
The time limit for a chat session
The list of websites the model was trained on
A saved history of all your past chats
questions.explanation: The context window holds the instructions, conversation, files and reply for one request. Anything outside it, the model cannot see.

questions.question: Why does a long chat start 'forgetting' things you said early on?
options: Older messages are dropped or summarized when the window fills up
The app deletes your messages after an hour
The model only reads the first message
questions.explanation: The full conversation is resent every turn. When it no longer fits, apps cut or summarize older messages, so those details are lost or shortened.

questions.question: A model has a very large context window. Which statement is true?
options: It will use every part of a long document equally well
It can see more text, but answers can still miss details buried in long inputs
questions.explanation: A big window means the text fits, not that the model pays equal attention to all of it. Sending only the relevant material still tends to give better answers.

questions.question: How is 'memory' different from the context window?
options: Memory is a few saved notes that get placed back into the context window in later conversations
Memory is unlimited and doesn't use tokens
questions.explanation: Memory features save key facts and put them back on the 'desk' at the start of a new chat. They still have to fit in the context window.
